Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your request, please see response from the Bike Unit: 
1. The bike lane on Flushing Ave in Brooklyn Navy Yard area (bikeid: 4463, prevbikeid: 1171) has the wrong retired/installed date. According to Google street view, the curbside bike lane became a sidewalk level bike lane somewhere between July 2019 and November 2020, the current install date however is 6/2/2022.

1. There are also numerous errors with the instdate column, with date going back to the early 1900s and 1930s, I'm certain that no bike lane was installed back then.

Inquiry:
On the recommendation of ***, I'm sending these questions here. I'd be extremely grateful for an opportunity to briefly interview the person managing the pension investment fund datasets:

1. While Period End Date specifies the end of the particular fiscal year, how can we determine at what date the decision to make a certain investment was made? 
2. What does Maturity Date specify? Is this when the investment being made starts to give returns? What is the timeline for when the returns from the respective investment also cease? Is this the date when the investment stopped earning interest? 
3. There is another date column in the dataset called  Date_as_of, what does that specify? The data dictionary has no explanation for this column.
4. From the dataset definitions, I understand that Original Face is the value of the investment when it was made, and the Base Total Cost is the amount of money the city had to pay out of pocket to buy the investments at original face value. Is this correct? If not, please explain the relationship between these two columns.
5. From the dataset definitions, I understand that Base Market Value specifies what the investment was worth in the market on the last day of the fiscal year. Which column of data specifies the exact amount of returns the pension fund received on the respective investment based on the decision to sell the asset? In addition, what is the best way of calculating how long the fund decided to hold certain investments and the one it has continued to hold for a long time (like more than a decade)? 
6. From the dataset definitions, I understand the Base Unrealized Gain/Loss, is calculated taking the Base Market Value (what it is worth now) and subtracting the Base Total Cost. But this would only indicate the "on paper" loss or gain from that investment. What would be the best method to determine the actual profitability of a certain investment?
Dataset Name: Office of The Comptroller: NYC Employee Retirement System (NYCERS) Holdings Data
Assigned Agency's Response:
Please find our response below:
 
1. While Period End Date specifies the end of the particular fiscal year, how can we determine at what date the decision to make a certain investment was made?
- Those data are not available in this dataset.
 
2. What does Maturity Date specify? Is this when the investment being made starts to give returns? What is the timeline for when the returns from the respective investment also cease? Is this the date when the investment stopped earning interest?
- A maturity date is the date on which a financial instrument reaches the end of its contractual life. At maturity, the obligations specified in the contract are settled, such as the repayment of principal, the final payment, or the completion of any remaining contractual commitments. For fixed income investments, the maturity date generally marks when the issuer repays the principal (or face value) to the investor and makes any final scheduled interest payment, after which the security ceases to exist. At maturity date, all gains and losses incurred by an investment during the holding are fully realized and, for interest-bearing instruments, interest no longer accrues. For other instruments, the maturity date is the date on which the contract expires or is settled according to its terms. Depending on the type of instrument, settlement may involve a cash payment, physical delivery of an underlying asset, or termination of the contract with no further obligations. 

3. There is another date column in the dataset called Date_as_of, what does that specify? The data dictionary has no explanation for this column.
- The “Data As Of” field in the file denotes the date at which the file was populated from the database. This is more of a version control tag: changes to any holdings attribute that occur between the Period End Date and the Data As Of date would be incorporated in this file.   

4. From the dataset definitions, I understand that Original Face is the value of the investment when it was made, and the Base Total Cost is the amount of money the city had to pay out of pocket to buy the investments at original face value. Is this correct? If not, please explain the relationship between these two columns.
- Original face amounts are fields populated specifically for pass-through securities. A unique feature of pass-through securities is that coupon payments include both principal and interest components. Hence, the underlying principal outstanding for the security declines over time. The original face is the original principal amount of a pass-through security at the time it is issued, before any principal has been repaid. It serves as the baseline against which future principal repayments and the remaining outstanding balance (shown in the Shares/Par Value field) are measured. The Base Total Cost field represents the total amount of money the investor paid for the instrument as of the Period End Date. These portfolios utilize an average costing method that takes into account all historical lots of a given position. In addition, the cost amount for fixed income securities may be adjusted for amortization/ accretion of discounts/premiums and for principal paydown activity on pass-through securities.

5. From the dataset definitions, I understand that Base Market Value specifies what the investment was worth in the market on the last day of the fiscal year. Which column of data specifies the exact amount of returns the pension fund received on the respective investment based on the decision to sell the asset? In addition, what is the best way of calculating how long the fund decided to hold certain investments and the one it has continued to hold for a long time (like more than a decade)?
- Base Market Value represents the amount an investor would expect to receive were they to liquidate the position in an orderly manner at the market close of the Period End Date. This amount is expressed in the portfolios’ base currency, USD. There are no fields available in the holdings file that report performance at the holdings level, given the variability of the input set and the amount of transaction-level and time-series data required to perform the calculation. Finally, data for the holding period of individual investments is not publicly available, nor can we disclose managers’ intent to buy, sell, or hold individual positions. 

6. From the dataset definitions, I understand the Base Unrealized Gain/Loss, is calculated taking the Base Market Value (what it is worth now) and subtracting the Base Total Cost. But this would only indicate the "on paper" loss or gain from that investment. What would be the best method to determine the actual profitability of a certain investment?
- That’s correct. The Base Unrealized Gain/Loss represents the unrealized gains attributed to each holding on the Period End Date, inclusive of currency gains & losses. To fully assess the performance of an investment over time, one would need to first define the period to be measured and then consider three components in the calculation: Income, Realized Gains, and Unrealized Gains. While it’s technically possible to aggregate the information necessary to calculate performance at the holdings level, it is not BAM’s practice to systematically do so for external managers and would balloon into a prohibitively large project if performed for all managers in the Plan.

I submitted a request in November 2025 for disaggregated reporting of DSNY tonnage data—specifically, four (4) separate monthly tonnage categories by sanitation district (curbside, containerized, school truck, and other), with each category reported across all four streams (refuse, paper, MGP, and organics).

To date, I have received no response. I have also heard informally that DSNY does not intend to implement this request. If that is the case, I respectfully request a formal response explaining the decision, with a level of detail commensurate with the original submission.

If the reluctance reflects operational changes—such as increased containerization of refuse in some districts or changes in school truck collection—I would welcome clarification on how these changes are currently represented in reported tonnage totals. My review of trends by material code in FOIL-released data suggests that such shifts may be relevant, but they are not transparent in the current dataset.

If DSNY has agreed to implement the request, in whole or in part, I would appreciate confirmation and information on the expected timeline for implementation.

***

Inquiry:
- Is there more information on the call type descriptions? For example, the difference between ARREST	and T-ARST is unclear as they have the same call type description. There are also some call types, such as MOSINJ and BPP, that are not in the data description.

- Is there more information on the severity level codes? For example, what is the difference between a 0 and a 9?

- Is there more information on the incident dispositions? For example, what is the difference between a patient pronounced dead and a patient gone on arrival?

- Is there more information on the dispatch area of the incident? For example, where exactly are M5 and K6? Also what is meant by dispatch area?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Question Asked:
- Is there more information on the call type descriptions? For example, the difference between ARREST and T-ARST is unclear as they have the same call type description. There are also some call types, such as MOSINJ and BPP, that are not in the data description.
Call Type Descriptions:
The Call Type field represents the nature of the incident as coded in the FDNY EMS Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system.
- Codes with the “T-” prefix (e.g., ARREST vs T-ARST) indicate that the call information was electronically transmitted/texted into CAD rather than entered through the standard voice-based 911 intake process.
- The prefix reflects a different dispatch workflow only; the underlying medical complaint and public description remain the same.
- Some call types such as MOSINJ and BPP are internal CAD codes associated with severity level 9 and are typically related to incidents marked “Out of Service.” These records are not part of the public Open Data dataset and therefore are not included in the posted data description file.

Question Asked:
- Is there more information on the severity level codes? For example, what is the difference between a 0 and a 9?
Severity Level Codes:
Severity codes reflect the dispatcher’s triage-based assessment of urgency at the time of call intake.
- Severity levels are generally ranked from 1 (most severe) to 8 (least severe), with 1–3 being life-threatening and 4–8 being non-life-threatening.

Question Asked:
- Is there more information on the incident dispositions? For example, what is the difference between a patient pronounced dead and a patient gone on arrival?
Incident Dispositions:
The Disposition field reflects the final outcome of the EMS response.
- Patient Pronounced Dead: EMS personnel determined that the patient was deceased at the scene according to formal protocol.
- Patient Gone on Arrival: EMS units arrived at the scene, but the patient was not present (e.g., the patient left before EMS arrival or could not be located).
- These outcomes are operationally distinct and represent different response results within standard EMS reporting.

Question Asked:
- Is there more information on the dispatch area of the incident? For example, where exactly are M5 and K6? Also what is meant by dispatch area?
Dispatch Area:
Dispatch Area refers to the internal operational response zone responsible for assigning EMS resources—not a precise patient address. The letter identifies the borough (M = Manhattan, K = Brooklyn/Kings, Q = Queens, X = Bronx, S/R = Staten Island), and the number identifies a specific EMS sector within that borough (e.g., M5 = Manhattan Zone 5; K6 = Brooklyn Zone 6).
Exact geographic boundaries of these zones are not included in the public dataset to protect patient privacy. Detailed maps and boundary definitions are maintained in FDNY EMS internal documentation.

Inquiry:
When I download the data as a CVS I retrieve more than 2300  records. But when I download as an API only the first 1000 are retrieved.
Is there a parameter that I need to set or reset?
Thank you
Assigned Agency's Response:
I'm Aryanna from the NYC Open Data Team, nice to meet you! By default, the API returns a maximum of 1,000 records per request. To retrieve more than that, you can use the following techniques:
1. Increase the Limit: You can increase the number of records returned by using the $limit parameter. For example, to request 50,000 records:  https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/abcd-1234.json?$limit=50000
2. Paginate Using $offset: To request additional records, pair $limit with $offset to paginate through the data. This will allow you to pull the data in chunks:
    a. First Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=0  
    b. Second Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=50000  	
3. Optimize Your Query: Before making large requests, it's helpful to filter your results using the $select, $where, and $order parameters. This reduces unnecessary records and improves query performance.  
For more information on query parameters and how to work with large datasets please consult the following articles:  
- The LIMIT Clause documentation (https://dev.socrata.com/docs/queries/limit.html)
- How to Query More Than 1000 Rows (https://support.socrata.com/hc/en-us/articles/202949268-How-to-query-more-than-1000-rows-of-a-dataset)

Inquiry:
Questions about joining tables.  I would like to join the following tables:
1.  Can the datasets 'NYPD Calls for Service' and the 'EMS incident Dispatch Data' be joined?  if so, what is the joining field/key?
2.   Can the 'EMS incident Dispatch Data' and the 'NYPD use of Force' dataset be joined?  if so, what is the joining field/key?
Thanks in advance.
Dataset Name: NYPD Calls for Service (Year to Date), EMS Incident Dispatch Data, NYPD Use of Force Incidents
Assigned Agency's Response:
These datasets cannot be cleanly joined because the versions published on NYC Open Data contain limited fields and no shared incident ID between NYPD and EMS.
 
1. NYPD Calls for Service ↔ EMS Incident Dispatch
- No direct join key. NYPD and FDNY use separate CAD systems, and the Open Data versions don’t include any matching incident numbers.
- PD isn’t involved in every EMS incident, so even an approximate join won’t capture all overlap.
- Only possible join is fuzzy (date/time + location), and even that will be inconsistent due to limited fields.
 
2. EMS Incident Dispatch ↔ NYPD Use of Force
- No common identifier in the Open Data versions.
- Use-of-force events may or may not involve EMS, and EMS data on Open Data does not include NYPD incident numbers.
- Again, only approximate joins using time + location, but with low reliability.
 
Not all PD incidents involve EMS and vice versa; and even when they do, similar information available in both tables on Open Data is not a guaranteed incident match

Inquiry:
I am requesting a change in the codes and categories used in the DSNY Monthly Tonnages dataset, a long-standing and widely used resource for understanding New York City’s waste generation and collection patterns.
In June 2025, there were revisions to this dataset to expand the range of collection types included in the Refuse, Paper, and MGP recycling categories. While broader reporting is welcome, the aggregation of Schools and Containerized/Special collections with Curbside collections into single lump-sum columns has reduced the dataset’s utility for both Open Data users and policymakers. Documentation of this problem is attached.
The proposed solution is straightforward: restore separate columns for Curbside, Schools, and Containerized/Special collections across all four material streams. This approach would:
- Align with DSNY’s existing internal reporting codes;
- Provide consistency across material categories; and
- Remain compatible with aggregated totals reported in other DSNY publications, including the Annual Report, Mayor’s Management Report, Zero Waste updates, and Solid Waste Management Plan documents.
- Preserve the agency’s goal to “to align with other DSNY published reports.”

Specifically, the curbside refuse should be code 01, Household Collection. School refuse should be code 81, School Trucks. And containerized other refuse should be all other codes. Curbside paper recycling should be code 31, school truck paper should be code 48, and all other codes should be containerized other paper. MGP tons should be code 33 for curbside, code 78 for school truck MGP, and all other MGP codes in containerized other.   Organics codes and categories are fine as is and don't need changes.
                    
Maintaining this level of detail is critical for accurate analysis, informed policymaking, and transparent public reporting. I appreciate NYC Open Data’s commitment to providing high-quality, actionable datasets, and believe the adjustments proposed here will enhance the value of DSNY Monthly Tonnages for all stakeholders.
Rationale:
1.     Under current aggregated reporting, calculating a capture rate for the curbside composting program, which is the nation’s largest and vastly outweighs schools or other small organics programs, is no longer possible because we can’t isolate curbside refuse tonnages in the denominator.  The same argument applies to curbside paper recycling and curbside MGP recycling capture rates.  
2.     Blending school tonnages with curbside and containerized tonnages prevents evaluation of school recycling and organics.  While I understand that not all schools are served only by school trucks for all streams, there is public value in reporting school truck collections, as evidenced by DSNY’s continuing reporting of school organics tonnages.
3.     The current method of reporting blends containerized collection data with school and curbside, making it impossible to track the progress of this distinct method of collection.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to your response and am happy to provide further clarification or examples if needed.
Respectfully submitted,
*****

Inquiry:
There are some parts of the data dictionary that are not clear:
- How do I interpret INITIAL_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CODE and  FINAL_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CODE?
- The description for the incident disposition codes are not clear to me. For example I am unsure what 90 (unfounded) means or 95 (triaged at scene no transport). I am also unsure about the difference between 87 (cancelled) and CANCEL (cancelled). I have a few more uncertainties, but I was wondering if there is a way I can get a more detailed description for all incident disposition codes?

Thank you in advance!
Assigned Agency's Response:
1. INITIAL_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CODE & FINAL_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CODE
- Initial severity: This indicates the severity of the incident at the time it is first assigned, based on information provided by the caller (i.e., the first severity assigned to the incident).
- Final severity: This reflects the severity determined after the response and assessment by EMS personnel, likely when the incident is closed.
- Severity levels are generally ranked from 1 (most severe) to 8 (least severe), with 1–3 being life-threatening and 4–8 being non-life-threatening.
- Differences between initial and final severity may occur for a variety of reasons, such as additional phone calls or assessments conducted on scene.
2. Incident Disposition Codes
Disposition codes reflect the outcome or resolution of the incident. Examples include:
- 90 (Unfounded): No actionable incident was found after investigation.
- 95 (Triaged at scene, no transport): EMS evaluated the patient at the scene, but transport was not required.
- 87 (Cancelled) / “CANCEL”: The incident was cancelled before EMS arrival or transport. Both numeric and text codes typically indicate the same outcome, there is NO differences between the two.

Inquiry: So some datasets you update daily, we want to be able to maintain this data on our end to fetch the freshest data. The API for fetching data only allows to fetch 1000 records at a time. Is there a way around that?
Assigned Agency's Response:
By default, the API returns a maximum of 1,000 records per request. To retrieve more than that, you can use any of the following techniques:  
1. Increase the Limit: You can increase the number of records returned by using the $limit parameter. For example, to request 50,000 records:  https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/abcd-1234.json?$limit=50000 
2. Paginate Using $offset: To request additional records, pair $limit with $offset to paginate through the data:  
    a. First Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=0  
    b. Second Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=50000  
					(This will allow you to pull the data in chunks.) 
1. Optimize Your Query: Before making large requests, it's helpful to filter your results using the $select, $where, and $order parameters. This reduces unnecessary records and improves query performance.  
For more information on query parameters and how to work with large datasets please consult the following articles:  
- The LIMIT Clause Documentation (https://dev.socrata.com/docs/queries/limit.html)
- How to Query More Than 1000 Rows (https://support.socrata.com/hc/en-us/articles/202949268-How-to-query-more-than-1000-rows-of-a-dataset)

Assigned Agency's Response:
FY2025 will be added to the dataset at the end of October or at the beginning of November.
 
The fiscal year ends on June 30th each year, and thus cannot be updated before that date. The data analysis for citywide pay is conducted only after the fiscal year ends. The results must be reviewed by various agencies to ensure that information regarding every confidential employee is removed and/or redacted. Inquiry: Is there any possibility to get all 4 million records? I use Xquery but it is limited to bring only 1000. Is there any possibility to get with out restriction ?
Assigned Agency's Response:
By default, the API returns a maximum of 1,000 records per request. To retrieve more than that, you can use the following techniques:
- Increase the Limit: You can increase the number of records returned by using the $limit parameter. For example, to request 50,000 records, you would use the following query: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/abcd-1234.json?$limit=50000 
- Paginate Using $offset: To request additional records, pair $limit with $offset to paginate through the data. This will allow you to pull the data in smaller batches:  
    - First Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=0  
    - Second Page: ?$limit=50000&$offset=50000  	
- Optimize Your Query: Before making large requests, it's helpful to filter your results using the $select, $where, and $order parameters. This reduces unnecessary records and improves query performance.  
For more information on query parameters and how to work with large datasets please consult the following articles:  
- The LIMIT Clause 
- How to Query More Than 1000 Rows

Inquiry:
Hello,
I am struggling to convert wkt point data or segment ID from the Traffic Volume Counts to Latitude Longitude format to input into ArcGIS Pro. I saw that the information is in lion, but which columns of the LION file can be used to create XY points in ArcGIS? Any other suggestions? I want to input the traffic data into ArcGIS Pro. 
Thanks.
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data on Automated Traffic Recorder dataset. Well-known text (WKT) represents coordinate reference systems in machine and human readable language. The dataset contains X, Y coordinates. You need a Geographic Information System (GIS) application to convert X,Y to Lat, Long coordinates such as ArcGIS or the open source QGIS.
1. Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
	1. Export data to CSV and format the WktGeom column (remove "POINT" and parentheses). Separate the X,Y into two columns (use the space as the break.)
	2. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add two new columns in the attribute table (long, lat).
	3. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
	a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
	b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
	c. Units: Decimal Degree
1. You may use ArcPy to convert the data into geometry, see information from ESRI below.
ArcPy function WKT: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/10.6/analyze/...
 
1. Using QGIS- free to download
2. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
3. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
	a. Format: CSV
	b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
	c. Layer Option- Geometry: AS_XY
Best, 
 Department of Transportation (DOT)

The Dept. of Correction serves to provide the care, custody and control of individuals awaiting trial or serving a sentence after being found guilty for misdemeanor charges (serving less than one year). Inquiry:
Hello,

I am interested in this dataset on traffic speeds for a research project I am conducting at the Computer Science Department at *****. Specifically, I am interested in gaining further understanding of the different columns of this dataset, and what the speed and travel_time columns represent - I looked in the metadata but still have questions about the length of the interval that each speed is calculated for, what the ID variables represent, and how many different sensors there are, among other questions.

Best,
*****
Assigned Agency's Response:
Apologies for the delay and thank you for your request with New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT). Additional information as follows:
- Data are captured and retained every one minute. 
- Each link_point, one set of Lat, Long coordinates (40.7714206, -73.83345), is a sensor. 
- The “speed” column captures the average travel speed in miles per hour between the beginning (first set of Lat, Long coordinates) and end (last set of Lat, Long coordinates) of “link_points”. 
- The “travel_time” represents the average travel time in seconds between the beginning and end of “link_points”. 
- There are link points between stretches to capture additional speed information and travel time (number of seconds between each link_points) used to calculate average speed and travel time. 
- The ID is associated with the Link_Name (location of the stretch). 
- 453 locations speeds have been captured, but there could be locations that have since retired.
We will update the metadata to include this additional information.
Visit NYC DOT Real Time Traffic Conditions and Cameras for more information. If you have any additional questions, feel free to reply to this email or contact NYC DOT via webform- choose topic Traffic Congestion . 
 Thank you,
Best,

Inquiry:
Hello, I have a question about the specific indication of individual buildings in New York City LL87 Energy Audit Data. I am trying to find for each individual building in this dataset, what is its annual cooling energy use? I am referring to the "Existing Annual Energy Use_Electricity_space cooling" column for this information. My question though is concerning the "BINs" column indicating the specific building described by each row in the dataset. I am confused about how to handle entries in this column that list multiple BIN IDs, separated by semicolons. How should I treat these? Does this mean that all of the audit data for that particular row applies equally to all BIN IDs (individual buildings) listed in the "BINs" column for that row? For understanding the annual cooling energy use for that row, how does this value get distributed across all of the listed BIN IDs for that row? If I have multiple BIN IDs listed for that row, then how do I know how much of that annual cooling energy consumption value for that row was used by each of the buildings listed for that row? I would rely on New York City LL84 Energy Benchmarking Data, but from my understanding this dataset only includes whole building energy use intensity (EUI), which would not help me understand specific end use energy consumption, specifically whole building space cooling energy consumption. Is this correct, or should I be looking at another column here? I would appreciate any help in understanding how I could leverage NYC OpenData building energy consumption data to know how I can understand the cooling energy use of individual buildings.

Thank you for your time
Assigned Agency's Response: Our understanding is that LL87 is reported by BBL. BBLs may contain only a single building or multiple buildings, denoted by BINs. If it contains only a single building (single BIN #), then there will be only one Energy Efficiency Report (EER) submission for that BBL. If there are multiple buildings (multiple BINs) for the BBL and they all share the same base building systems then there will still only be one EER for that BBL, and all energy data applies to all buildings comprehensively. If there are multiple buildings but they each have their own base building systems then a separate EER will need to be submitted for each building (each BIN) and the energy data reported applies only to the individual building (individual BIN). Base building systems include: the building envelope, HVAC (Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning) systems, conveying systems, domestic hot water systems, and electrical and lighting systems.

Inquiry: I'd like to know more about the data collection process. Is this reported by the pantries/kitchens? And to confirm, this is report is duplicative (i.e., individuals may be counted as many times as they visit a pantry/kitchen)?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Both the ‘individuals served’ at food pantries and the ‘meals served’ at soup kitchens are self-reported and reflect the duplicated persons served by CFC-funded programs:
1. The number of individuals served by CFC-funded food pantries represents the total served by the food pantry based on the family size. This figure is duplicated meaning that individuals served are counted more than once depending on the number of visits. For example, if one person is picking up a pantry bag for a family of four, the pantry will record that four individuals were served. If that same family received another pantry bag that month, the pantry would record that eight individuals were served, etc. 
2. Soup kitchens are able to convert persons served to meals as each individual served represents one meal; again, this is a duplicated figure as an individual can be served at a soup kitchen multiple times in a month. 
 
The number of individuals served at food pantries and meals served at soup kitchens are reporting the same ‘Total Service’ measure that reflects the number of duplicated individuals served in a month, with pantries using the family size to count the number served and the soup kitchens counting the number of meals/individuals served.

Inquiry:
Hi there, I hope this email finds you well! I'm part of a team of researchers at ***** using Open Data's "Automated Traffic Volume Counts" dataset, and I believe we've found a major discrepancy in the data that has been uploaded to the site, which we wanted to alert Open Data to.

We have used this dataset for various research projects between 2022 and 2024. Last March I sent a request through this form asking for this data to be updated as it had been dormant since December 2022 (Inquiry ID #10761). A representative from NYC DOT promptly reached out and told me the dataset had been updated.

This was greatly appreciated by me and others using this dataset. However, we immediately noticed discrepancies between the updated dataset and the previous version. The current full dataset (which should include data from 2000 to 2023) has 1,673,725 rows. The previous dataset, in contrast, included 27,190,511 rows despite being an older dataset.

Investigating the cause of this further in R, we identified a significant number of streets in the old dataset that are completely absent from the new dataset. In Queens alone, for the year 2020, there are records for 90 unique streets in the old dataset, but only 10 unique streets in the new dataset, despite supposedly having 1 year's worth of new data, in addition to previously recorded data.

This is just one example of a discrepancy between the two sets. Due to the large volume of data we could not narrow down the exact differences between both versions. Inquiry:
the columns sign_x_coord and sign_y_coord are documented as longitude, latitude. However, the data provided doesn't seem to be valid. latitude ranges from -90 to 90, and longitude -180 to 180.

Example:
1006449, 219326

So how do I convert sign_x_coord and sign_y_coord to longitude, latitude values?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your request on Parking Regulation Sign locations. The coordinate system for the signs are in X,Y, you will need to convert to Latitude and Longitude. One method is to use a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) system application like ArcMap or QGIS, note: some basic GIS knowledge required.
ArcMap-:
1. Download the data as CSV or shapefile
2. If using CSV, load the data into the application as a CSV. Or load the shapefile.
3. Right click on the layer to open an attribute table. Add two new columns in the attribute table, "Lat", "Long".
4. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

QGIS-: Free and Open Source
1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
3. a. Format: CSV
4. b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
5. c. Layer Option- Geometry: AS_XY

Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation

Charge 1 Infraction amount

For example, summons number 000766944Y has the following values

Inquiry: The location of street signs on this dataset (sign_x_coord, sign_y_coord) are given in a unque format (e.g. "sign_x_coord": "1033748", "sign_y_coord": "195599"). What is this coordinate system? How can I convert those coordinates into standard format of DEGREES, MINUTES, AND SECONDS (DMS)? Thank you.
Assigned Agency's Response:
The Parking Regulation Locations and Signs dataset offers X,Y coordinate system in the tracking system, the coordinates you've requested are in decimal degree, which are Latitude and Longitude. Example: "sign_x_coord": "1033748", "sign_y_coord": "195599" is converts to Latitude: 40.7034, Longitude: -73.8215
A Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software can be used to convert these coordinates, using ESRI ArcGIS or the free open-source platform QGIS, some basic application knowledge is required, see options below.
1) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree
Additional information: More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).

2) Using QGIS- free to install
More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conv...
To do:
1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
a. Format: CSV
b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
c. Layer Option- Geometry: AS_XY 
d. Ok
Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation

Inquiry:
Hello,

The stop, frisk, and search data from 2017 to 2022 include “STOP_WAS_INITIATED”. The column includes three elements: Based on Self Initiated, Based on Radio Run, and Based on C/W on Scene.

Based on my understanding, each element can be defined as below.
Based on Self Initiated – Police officers initiated police stops without a warrant in hand.
Based on Radio Run – Police officers engaged in police stops after communicating with dispatchers.
Based on C/W on Scene – Police officers engaged in police stops after communicating with cooperating witnesses on scene.

Question1: Would you please confirm whether my understandings are correct? If possible, would you provide any document that includes more detailed information on each element?

The stop, frisk, and search data prior to 2017 do NOT include “STOP_WAS_INITIATED” but instead include the “radio” column (Yes/No).
Question 2: Is “Yes” equivalent to “Based on Radio Run” in the 2017-2022 data? Does "No" indicate “Based on Self Initiated” and “Based on C/W on Scene” in the 2017-2022 data?

Thank you for the help.
Dataset Name: The Stop, Question and Frisk Data
Assigned Agency's Response:
Question 1: Would you please confirm whether my understandings are correct? If possible, would you provide any document that includes more detailed information on each element?

Your assessment of the data variables are mostly correct, but there are many facts and circumstances that may lead a police officer to conclude that there is reasonable suspicion that a person has committed, is committing or is about to commit a felony or Penal Law misdemeanor. Such factors may include information received from third parties as well as the actions of the suspect, the suspect’s physical and temporal proximity to the scene of a crime, the suspect’s resemblance to the specific description of a perpetrator of a crime (based on more than just race, age and gender) and information known to the officer about the suspect or particular location, among other factors. Each situation is unique and the information available to members of the service will vary.


Question 2: Is “Yes” equivalent to “Based on Radio Run” in the 2017-2022 data? Does "No" indicate “Based on Self Initiated” and “Based on C/W on Scene” in the 2017-2022 data?

The SQF data prior to 2017 contains 2 data variables that can be used to gather additional information regarding the source of the information for a stop. Column #42 "radio" has a value of 'Y' or 'N' which indicates whether the stop was based upon a call from the police dispatcher. Column # 43 "ac_rept" has a value of 'Y' or 'N" which indicates whether the stop was based upon a report by a victim, witness or a police officer.



Thank you,
NYC Open Data Team

Inquiry:
What coordinate system has been used for these coordinates? I know the format is WKT, but the values for longitude and latitude are confusing to me.

Kind regards,
Merel
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting the Open Data HelpDesk regarding WKT field for the Automated Traffic Volume Counts data. This field contains X,Y coordinates and not the common Lat, Long coordinates. You will need a GIS application to make the conversion, such as ArcMap or QGIS (open source).
Helpful guides- some basic GIS knowledge is required:
1) ArcMap- use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
2) ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).
To do:
1. Remove the parentheses for the WKT and separate the numbers (before and after the space) into LAT column and Long column.
2. Load the data into the GIS application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (lat,and long).
3. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

3) QGIS- free to download, more information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conv...
To do:
1) Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2) Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
a. Format: CSV
b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
c. Geometry: AS_XY
Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation

Inquiry:
1. Does the dataset cover all parks within NYC, regardless of their management/ownership—whether federal, state, city, or non-profit organizations? Or is it limited to parks under the city's ownership or management?

2. Does the "acquisition date" indicate the date the park property was officially acquired by the city government?

3. Is there a distinction between the "acquisition date" and the year a park was established? If so, could you elucidate the difference?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Please see the responses to your questions below. If you have any follow up questions, you can reach out to *****.
 
1. Acquisition date refers to the date it came under NYC Park’s jurisdiction/management. When it is private property acquired for a park purpose, the acquisition date and the title vesting date is the same. We acquire property that is often already city-owned, and perhaps used initially for a different purpose, in that case the acquisition date still only reflects the date our agency took control of the parcel.
2. Jurisdiction refers to management, it may have nothing to do with the land acquisition process. For instance, land for jointly-operated playgrounds was usually acquired for school and park purposes. The land acquisition process was approved by the other government bodies, typically the Board of Estimate (BOE) up until the early 1980s, after consulting with NYC Parks. Upon the BOE’s approval, the City’s Law Department would acquire the property through whatever legal channels necessary, and upon vesting title, the land came under the control of the Department of Education and NYC Parks to execute the purpose for which the parcel was acquired. In other instances, NYC Parks may directly seek out a parcel of land for a park-related purpose and lobby for its acquisition with elected officials, community stakeholders, and seek official city authorization to acquire through the acquisition process outlined on our website, ULURP.
3. If a parcel is acquired through a negotiated purchase with a private entity, a council member may choose to allocate funding towards that acquisition. If funding has already been secured by other means, the Council’s role in the ULURP process is to either vote on the action or allow it to pass by taking no action. The roles of the Council, the City Planning Commission, the community board, the borough president, and mayor’s in the ULURP process are outline on City Planning’s website here: https://www.nyc.gov/site/planning/applicants/applicant-portal/step5-ulurp-process.page
 
Thanks,
NYC Parks Open Data Team

Inquiry: I am hoping to know what coordinate reference system is used to generate the WktGeom column? It is not listed in the data dictionary and is different than that used in the other datasets I've used from NYC OpenData. Thanks!
Assigned Agency's Response:
Apologies for the delay. Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data on Automated Traffic Recorder dataset. Well-known text (WKT) represents coordinate reference systems in machine and human readable language. The dataset contains X, Y coordinates. You need a GIS application to convert X,Y to Lat, Long coordinates such as ArcGIS or the open source QGIS.

) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
1. Export data to CSV and format the WktGeom column (remove "POINT" and parentheses). Separate the X,Y into two columns (use the space as the break.)
2. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add two new columns in the attribute table (long, lat).
3. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

2) You may use ArcPy to convert the data into geometry, see information from ESRI below.
ArcPy function WKT: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/10.6/analyze/...

3) Using QGIS- free to download

1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
3. a. Format: CSV
4. b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
5. c. Layer Option- Geometry: AS_XY
Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation

Inquiry:
Hi NYC Open Data,
I've been working with this dataset and observed that most of the sections of piers or reclaimed land in the East River off the west coastline of Brooklyn are labeled as being a part of the Manhattan borough. The sections are south of the Brooklyn Bridge, and west of Brooklyn Heights and the Columbia Waterfront. There are also a few docks or piers west of Williamsburg.

I've searched online to try to find more information about this and haven't found anything.

I assume these may be labeled in this way because of a policy or agreement that defines everything west of the Brooklyn coastline (all area of the East River) is part of Manhattan, and these sections fall within those boundaries or requirements.

Interestingly, most of Brooklyn Bridge Park is considered part of Manhattan, but other developed waterfront areas like John Street Park are not.

I'm curious to know more about the history of this if it is not an error, or of documents where these rules are defined. Do you know why these sections that are physically connected with Brooklyn are labeled as part of Manhattan?
Assigned Agency's Response:
This is not an error, the Borough Boundaries extend into the waterways and are defined in the City Charter (https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/newyorkcity/latest/NYCadmin/0-0-0-94).  The Manhattan boundary extends to the "low-water mark on the shore of Long Island" so you will also notice this for any piers in Queens along the East River.

The borough of Manhattan shall consist of the territory known as New York county... thence across the East river to the low-water mark on the shore of Long Island, so as to include Randall's Island and Ward's Island; thence along the low-water mark on the shore of Long Island to the southerly side of Red Hook; thence across the Upper bay to the westerly boundary of the state...

Inquiry:
What is the coordinate reference system used by the column WktGeom? Is there any way I can transform it into Latitude and longitude? And is there another dataset for segmentID and Latitude-longitude informations?

Best regards,
Cleon
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data regarding Automated Traffic Recorder dataset.
SegmentID are unique IDs assigned to each New York City street block by the NYC Department of City Planning, the information can be found in the LION dataset, and you may use that field to join with the
Automated Traffic Volume Counts dataset.
LION data: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/LION...
Well-known text (WKT) represents coordinate reference systems in machine and human readable language. The dataset contains X,Y coordinates. You may also search mapping WktGeom or convert the coordinates from X,Y to Lat, Long using Geographic Information System (GIS) applications. Examples of GIS applications are ESRI ArcGIS, ArcPy or the free open-source platform QGIS, some basic application knowledge is required, see options below:

A) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).
To do:
1) Export data to CSV and format the WktGeom column (remove "POINT" and parentheses). Separate the X,Y into two columns (use the space as the break.)
2. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (long and lat).
3. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

B) You may use ArcPy to convert the data into geometry, see information from ESRI below.
ArcPy function WKT: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/10.6/analyze/...
ESRI GIS forum: https://community.esri.com/t5/python-questions/exp...

C) Using QGIS- free to download
More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conv...

To do:
1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
3. a. Format: CSV
4. b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
5. c. Geometry: AS_XY

Inquiry: I exported the csv file from the dataset URL and see the x and y coordinates for each of the raised crosswalks, is there any way I can get the Latitude and Longitude for these points to map them either in google maps or google earth?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your inquiry. The Raised Crosswalk Locations data provides only X and Y coordinates. You may use a Geographic Information System (GIS) applications such as ESRI ArcGIS or the free open-source platform QGIS to process X,Y conversion to Latitude (lat), Longitude (long). Some basic GIS application knowledge is required, see information below:

1) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).

To do:
1. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (long and lat).
2. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

2) Using QGIS- free to download
More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conv...

To do:
1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
3. a. Format: CSV
4. b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
5. c. Geometry: AS_XY

Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation

Inquiry: The "wktgeom" column it gives coordinates. What is the "Coordinate Reference System" for these points?(i.e. epsg:4269)
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your inquiry. The Automated Traffic Volume Counts dataset contains X,Y coordinates. You may also search mapping WktGeom or convert the coordinates from X,Y to Lat, Long using Geographic Information System (GIS) applications. Examples of GIS applications are ESRI ArcGIS or the free open-source platform QGIS, some basic application knowledge is required, see options below:

1) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage...
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).
To do:
1. Export data to CSV and format the WktGeom column (remove "POINT" and parentheses). Separate the X,Y into two columns (use the space as the break.)
2. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (long and lat).
3. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

2) Using QGIS- free to download
More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conv...

To do:
1. Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
2. Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
3. a. Format: CSV
4. b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
5. c. Geometry: AS_XY

Thank you,
NYC Department of Transportation, NYC Open Data Team

Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your inquiry. Unfortunately, the Parking Regulation and Location Sign system only provides X and Y coordinates. New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) maintains a website for all New York City Parking Regulation Signs mapped, please visit: https://nycdotsigns.net/. You may also use Geographic Information System (GIS) applications such as ESRI ArcGIS or the free open-source platform QGIS to process X,Y conversions to Lat, Long, some basic application knowledge is required, see information below:1) Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website: https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage-data/tables/calculating-area-length-and-other-geometric-properties.htm
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).
To do:
1. Load the data into the application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (long and lat).
2. Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

2) Using QGIS- free to download
More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conversion-process-in-qgis.html

To do:
Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file) Fill in as follows:
a. Format: CSV
b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
c. Geometry: AS_XY

Thank you,

Inquiry:
1. I wonder why most rows of the 'Fluoride' column have missing values(empty string). Does it mean those sites have 0 Fluoride?

2. Can you explain more on the 'Sample.Class'? What's the difference of 'Compliance' and 'Operational'? And what does the 'Resample' ones mean?

Thanks!
Dataset Name: Drinking Water Quality Distribution Monitoring Data
Assigned Agency's Response:
To answer your questions in order:

1. No. Only a subset of the daily samples are analyzed for Fluoride which include the entry points to the distribution system. The other sites/samples are Not Analyzed but are assumed to have similar levels to the values found at the entry points.
2. As stated in the Data Dictionary, copied below, not all data are used for Compliance. The other data are collected for Operational purposes but results are provided in OpenData. As required by the Total Coliform Rule, when a sample is positive for coliform at a Compliance site a set of Resamples must be collected from the location. For Operational sites it is only one resample.

Please note: Data are collected under the federal Revised Total Coliform Rule (RTCR) for compliance. All samples are collected and analyzed by DEP staff from fixed sample stations throughout drinking water distribution system. Data are used to assess the effectiveness of drinking water treatment in accordance with the requirements of federal and state rules and regulations. But not all data presented are used to determine / calculate compliance with the regulations.

Thank you,
- NYC DEP Open Data

Inquiry:
Is it possible to calculate a property's tax bill directly from the PLUTO data?

Assigned Agency's Response:
The Department of City Planning (DCP) published PLUTO/MapPLUTO. Most of its source data, including assessed values, comes from the Department of Finance (DOF).  For any field in PLUTO, please make sure to read the data dictionary so you understand how the values for that field are collected and/or processed.

This is what is listed for all data related to all "Assessed Values," the Department of Finance (DOF) calculates the assessed value by multiplying the tax lot’s estimated full market value by a uniform percentage for the property’s tax class. Property value is assessed as of January 5th. If a new building is not completed by April 14th, the assessed building value is 0 and the Building Class reverts to Vacant. Assessed and exempt values are updated twice a year. Tentative values are released in mid-January and final values are released around May 25. If the date on source file (PTS), as reported in the Readme file, is between January 15 and May 25, ASSESSED TOTAL VALUE is from the tentative roll for the tax year starting in July. Otherwise, ASSESSED TOTAL VALUE is from the final roll.
For further questions about determining the applicable tax percent you would have to reach out to the Department of Finance (DOF).

Thank you,

8/31/22 Follow Up Question: Can you explain to me or possibly direct me to a resource to understand what the updates mean pertaining to data vs meta-data? I don't understand what a 2022 update to 17-18 data means? Has it necessarily changed? Better understanding this would help me to use data via NYC Open Data overall. Thank you.
Assigned Agency's Response:
This dataset contains data on the 2017-2018 school year.  Under the "About this Dataset" section, note that there are different timestamps for when the Data was last updated and when the Metadata was last updated.  Hope this helps!

Thank you,

-----
Follow-up
Sure thing!

“Data Last Updated” means the date on which the data itself was altered in some way. Examples of this can include:
The removal of one or more records
Changing the values in one or more fields (e.g. fixing a misspelled word)
Adding new records when new data is available
“Metadata Last Updated” means the date on which the metadata was altered in some way. Metadata can be defined as data/information about data. On the Open Data Portal, metadata is found in the “About this Dataset” section on a dataset’s primer page. Examples of altering the metadata can include:
Uploading new versions of data documentation (e.g. data dictionaries and readme files)
Changing any field of “Dataset Information” (e.g. changing the update frequency, changing the category, or switching which Agency a dataset belongs to)
The general “Updated” date changes when either the data or metadata has been updated.

You can find out more here: https://support.socrata.com/hc/en-us/articles/221691947-Data-Insights-Primer-a-dataset-s-landing-page. Hope this helps!

Thank you,

Inquiry: HI. I have filtered this dataset how i want it and are trying to plot the data in google maps, but the coordinate system EPSG:2263 does not work in google maps. I then tried to use your own visualizations, but this too needs lat long. I used a Javascript to convert them but then it needs to be imbedded in a site for the java to run and I don't want that just a simple kml
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for your inquiry. Unfortunately, the Street Sign Work Orders system does not provide latitude (lat) and longitude (long) information, only X,Y.  A possible solution is to use Geographic Information System (GIS) applications such as ESRI ArcGIS or the free open-source platform QGIS to process the conversions, some basic application knowledge is required, see information below:
Using ArcGIS- license required
Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table. More information about the tool on the ArcGIS website:https://desktop.arcgis.com/en/arcmap/latest/manage-data/tables/calculating-area-length-and-other-geometric-properties.htm
ESRI community forum (https://community.esri.com/t5/arcgis-api-for-flex-questions/how-to-convert-x-y-to-lat-long/td-p/353854).
To do:
1.  Load the data into the application as a CSV, add new columns in the attribute table (long and lat).
2.  Use the Calculate Geometry tool in the attribute table (right click on the column header) to process the conversion. Fill in as follows:
a. Coordinates system of the data sources: NAD1983 State Plane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
b. Use coordinate system of the data frame: WGS 1984
c. Units: Decimal Degree

Using QGIS- free to download

More information from this blog: https://www.gisoutlook.com/2020/05/coordinate-conversion-process-in-qgis.html

To do:
Import CSV file: Layer -> Add Layer -> Add Delaminated Text Layer (CSV file)-> (keep everything else as default) only change Geometry CRS: EPSG:2263- NAD83/ New York Long Island (ftUS) -> add
Export layer+ Conversion: Export-> Save Feature As-> File Name: (select where to save the new file)  Fill in as follows:
a. Format: CSV
b. CRS: EPSG:4326- WGS 84
c. Geometry: AS_XY
Thank you,
- NYC DOT Open Data Team

Assigned Agency's Response:
There are multiple reasons for the issues that you noticed. Due to the rollout of a new system to handle 311 service requests in September 2021, a number of old complaint types were deprecated and merged with new complaint types. For example, “Dirty Conditions” that existed before is now only known as “Dirty Condition”. The descriptors associated with complaints have also been deprecated, and some don’t exist anymore.

The Department of Sanitation is currently working with DoITT (the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications) to figure out a technical solution to connect the old and new complaint types so that historical comparisons can be made. Once the data is corrected by DoITT, the 311 datasets will have to be republished. We cannot provide a timeframe when this will happen since we do not control this process.

Please note that the Scorecard Inspection program, which measures and reports on street and sidewalk cleanliness across the city’s five boroughs, is a program managed through the Mayor’s Office of Operations (not the Department of Sanitation) so you will need to direct your questions regarding this program to them. Here is a link to the webpage that contains the latest Scorecard Inspection reports: https://www1.nyc.gov/site/operations/performance/scorecard-street-sidewalk-cleanliness-ratings.page.

I hope you find this information helpful.

Inquiry: What does x-coord or y-coord represent? I was trying to render the data on the map, but they were not long/lat geometry data. Also, how can I convert them into long/lat?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Hi Minjung Sim,

Thank you for your inquiry. The X, Y coordinates (State Plane) in the data are created by a Mapping and Analytics Software, ex: ESRI- ArcGIS. A similar or same software is also needed to convert the X,Y coordinates to Lat, Long. The coordinates vary based on the location and the mapping projection of the data. The following X,Y coordinates conversion directions are for ArcGIS- ArcMap using the following projection:

Projected Coordinate System: NAD_1983_StatePlane_New_York_Long_Island_FIPS_3104_Feet
Projection: Lambert_Conformal_Conic

Steps are also on the official ESRI ArcGIS website: https://support.esri.com/en/technical-article/000008944

1) Export the data on the Open Data Portal into CSV
2) Importing the CSV into ArcGIS- ArcMap
3) Display X,Y data from the CSV
4) A new temporary file will be created to display the X,Y
6) Export the temporary file data into shapefile
7) Open the attribute table for the newly saved shapefile
8) Add two new columns (Add Field).
9) Use the Calculate Geometry function in the attributes table to convert X,Y to Lat, Long.
- Use Coordinates System: NAD 1983 StatePlane New York Long Island FIPS 3104 Feet
- Units: Decimal Degrees
Thank you,
- NYC DOT Open Data Team

Assigned Agency's Response:
That data was created and released by the  New York City Panel on Climate Change (NPCC). The Department of City Planning (DCP) published the data on NPCC's behalf.

You can read more about the NPCC 2015 Report here: https://nyaspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/nyas.12593.
The metadata is embedded in the GIS data and available here: https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/data-maps/open-data/slr_metadata.pdf?r=1.

This GIS dataset is provided to enable users to assess future coastal flood risk. In particular, the data show areas of New York City that are potentially vulnerable to future flooding at high tide due to sea level rise under a range of model-based scenarios for the 2020s, 2050s, 2080s, and 2100.

This geodatabase includes layers showing the projected extent of future mean higher high water (MHHW) with sea level rise. Extents are based on local sea level rise projections released by the New York City Panel on Climate Change in 2015. The data include the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 90th percentile projections for the 2020s, 2050s, 2080s, and 2100. The data illustrate the scale of potential flooding, not the exact location, and do not account for erosion, rapid subsidence, or future construction. Feature classes are contained to NYC municipal boundaries and are not reliable for areas outside of NYC.

Thank you,
- DCP Open Data Team

Inquiry: In the NYC taxi dataset, is data for companies such as Uber, Lyft, etc. included in both, FHV and High Volume FHV, data files or just one? If it's in both the data files, will same trips be included in both and double-counted or do these datasets consist of different trips?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for reaching out to TLC Open Data.
TLC maintains several trip datasets, and trips are not double counted across the lists. Uber and Lyft (and previously Via and Juno) are classified as High Volume For-Hire Services (HVFHS) because they make over 10,000 trips per day, and their trips would be in those HVFHS trip tables. Yellow Medallion Taxi, Green SHL, and FHV trips are all separate lists. While vehicles can sometimes work across various platforms and industry sectors, their trips are assigned to the industry sector for which they were dispatched. For example: an FHV might be dispatched by a local community livery base for a trip and that trip would be included in our FHV trip records. That same car might later make a trip for Uber and that trip would be included in our HVFHS trip table.
Please feel free to reach out directly to odc@tlc.nyc.gov if you have any additional questions.
Best,
Ted
NYC Open Data & NYC TLC

Inquiry: What action is completed for some applicants to have a list agency code / description and some do not? As well as the request date. Is this information updated once called for a hiring pool?
Assigned Agency's Response:
The "List Agency Code" column indicates whether the list certification pertains to an Open Competitive exam or a Promotional exam. If the value in the field is "000", the list certification pertains to an Open Competitive exam, where candidates may be called by any agency with openings in the title. If the value in the field is a three-digit agency code, the list certification pertains to a Promotional exam, where candidates may be called for promotional openings at the agency in which they are employed.

The "Request Date" column reflects the date on which an agency submits a request to DCAS for names of candidates on the list who are eligible for appointment to an open position or positions.

The information on the Civil Service List Certification dataset does not pertain to actions taken by individual agencies following a certification, such as calling applicants to a hiring pool.

Thank you,
- NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services

Inquiry: I'm seeing apparent duplicates in this data. I downloaded the sheet and found over 5,000 entries that had the same incident key (and time, location, etc). The only difference between those duplicates are the victims listed. It seems to me that this data better represents the number of shooting victims, not incidents. Do you agree? I'm curious to learn what the methodology is and if I've misread the data. Thanks for your help!
Assigned Agency's Response:
The Shootings Open Data dataset contains a many-to-many relational structure with regard to shooting incident victims and perpetrators. In most cases where the relationship between perpetrator and victim is one-to-many or many-to-one the results are often coherent. In these cases there will be a unique incident identifier and with a singular perpetrator and records of identical demographic data and many victims with varying demographic data (or vice versa). Most of the time it is apparent in which direction the records relate to each other and a general count of victims or perpetrators can be discerned. Things can become confusing in situations where incidents involve many perpetrators and many victims. The issue is further compounded when some victims in a single incident are murdered and others are not.



For example, we may have an individual incident within the dataset that provides twenty-four records containing victim and perpetrator demographic information under a single incident ID. These records are only unique when all variables are considered. Multiplicity inherent in the relational structure results in a degree of redundancy and an accurate count of perpetrators and victims cannot be discerned. The data can only demonstrate the ages, races and sexes of those victims and perpetrators concerned but not how many individuals are involved. The reality of the incident is reflective of four perpetrators and three victims, one of whom was murdered. The individuals involved in the incident look like this:



Perpetrator-1

Perpetrator-2

Perpetrator-3

Perpetrator-4

Victim-1-Murder

Victim-2-Non-Murder

Victim-3-Non-Murder



The data yielded in the Open Data set is confounding because it reflects a separate record for every possible relational outcome. So, Perpetrator-1 has six total records. One for each victim – making three -- which are then repeated for the statistical murder flag that generates an affirmative and negative value for each since Perpetrator-1 was involved in both the murder and non-murder aspects of the incident. The same applies for Perpetrators-2 through 4, generating four perpetrator groups of six records each, totaling twenty-four records, all under the same unique incident ID. The resulting twenty-four records provide little insight into the nature of the individuals involved due to anonymization measures that obscure identifying traits of each individual.



Thank you,
- NYC Open Data Team

Inquiry:
My colleagues and I have noticed the spelling of Mariners Harbor in Staten Island is different in two NYC OpenData datasets. Your spelling is "Mariner's Harbor" with the apostrophe. From what I can tell, U.S.G.S., NOAA and NYC DoITT all spell it without the apostrophe. Is there are reason for your apostrophe or is it a typo? It's quite a mystery!
Thanks for your help.
Assigned Agency's Response:
The Department of City Planning (DCP) created a map in 2014 called New York: A City of Neighborhoods and two datasets were released as a result of the map and open data laws, Neighborhood Names and Places (fka Areas of Interest). These were not meant to be a comprehensive nor an official list of neighborhoods. The neighborhood names were mostly taken from our Neighborhood Tabulation Areas (NTA) dataset, which listed Mariner's Harbor as an NTA. The source for that spelling came from the 1969 Plan for NYC. Since the release of that dataset in 2014 DCP has also observed several modern sources using different versions of that neighborhood name with and without the apostrophe, both public (NYCHA, Parks Dept., NYPL, USPS) and private (google maps, apple maps, waze, etc.).

DCP has decided that we will drop the apostrophe and use Mariners Harbor when we release our updated Neighborhood Tabulation Areas (NTA) dataset later this year. The Neighborhood Names dataset will also be updated to include this change and any others related to the NTA update.


Thank you,
- DCP Open Data Team

The Health Department receives electronic laboratory reports for a number of infectious diseases, including COVID-19, as required by law in the NYC Health Code. When a specimen is collected from a patient who is a NYC resident for SARS-CoV-2 laboratory testing, the laboratory must report all results, whether positive, negative, or inconclusive, to the Health Department. So the citywide percent positivity is derived from all persons tested in NYC.


Thank you,

Inquiry: I have observed that this dataset does not cover all the parcels of a borough. For Manhattan, tax assessment was done for 1.3M Parcels and In Zoning there are only 42.4k Tax Lots. Does Tax Lot differ Parcels in this case ? and if Yes can you explain how could we match those Parcels the zoning?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Original Question: I have observed that this dataset does not cover all the parcels of a borough. For Manhattan, tax assessment was done for 1.3M Parcels and In Zoning there are only 42.4k Tax Lots. Does Tax Lot differ Parcels in this case ? and if Yes can you explain how could we match those Parcels the zoning?

There are less than one million tax lots in NYC - you can verify that in MapPLUTO or DTM. I think this discrepancy is related to condos and condo lots. For every condominium building in the city there is a base lot for the building (usually begins with a 7500 number) and then each individual condo unit receives a condo lot number (usually in the 1000-1999 range). Therefore, PLUTO and the Zoning Tax Lot Database would have less lots (parcels) than a dataset the includes individual condo lots, That still seems too high to have 1.3 million parcels in only Manhattan.

If you want to follow up please email DCPOpenData@planning.nyc.gov.

Thank you,
- DCP Open Data Team

Inquiry:
Hi! Just a quick question-- in the fhv trip data, do pickup times reflect when when the passenger requested a ride, or when the passenger entered the vehicle/was actually picked up?

Assigned Agency's Response:
Hi,

Thank you for reaching out about the TLC's FHV Trip Records. The pickup time field, as it is laid out in our data reporting specifications, is supposed to capture the moment the trip begins, not the time of the request. For the four app-based For-Hire Vehicle bases (Uber, Lyft, Via, and Juno) whose interfaces capture this information, we expect the pickup time to be fairly exact. For smaller traditional car service companies, it is possible that these times reflect estimates. Trip records for small bases are often transcribed from notes after a trip is completed.

For more field descriptions, you can view the app-based data reporting specifications here:
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/Businesses/bases/hvfhs_data_reporting_specifications_2019-06-05.xlsx

and the traditional FHV base data reporting instructions here:
https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/csv_instruction_manual_december2018_final.pdf

Please note that all fields in the two data reporting specifications that are not currently released to the public through Open Data are exempt under FOIL. Hope this is helpful!

Best,
NYC Open Data + Taxi and Limousine Commission
