1. What are bases? Do app companies such as Uber or Lyft own these bases in the form of LLCs, or are they having partnerships with other firms?

2. Are bases decided by locations of NYC? Can there be any overlap in their coverage?

3. What are the relationships between bases and rental service companies?

We apologize if we have caused any inconvenience.
But we believe this data provides us such an excellent opportunity to understand and study the taxi industry, and we sincerely hope that our questions can be solved.

Thank you so much for the reading.

With Best Wishes
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for reaching out about for-hire vehicle trip records. I have answered your questions below.

1. What are bases? Do app companies such as Uber or Lyft own these bases in the form of LLCs, or are they having partnerships with other firms?
- Bases are businesses licensed by the Taxi and Limousine Commission to dispatch TLC-licensed drivers to passengers throughout NYC. Whereas yellow taxis can pick up passengers on the basis of a street-hail, a black car, luxury limo, or community car service must be dispatched by a base. Before apps like Uber and Lyft became available, this arrangement was traditionally done over the phone. Because New York had existing laws about for-hire vehicles when Uber and Lyft became available, those companies were required to get base licenses in order to operate in New York. The bases listed in the trip record guide are owned by the app companies, not operated by partners. On August 14, 2018, the TLC created a new license type for bases doing more than 10,000 trips per day, the High Volume For-Hire Vehicle license, so Uber, Lyft, Via, and Juno's bases are now legally distinct from traditional for-hire vehicle bases and have different reporting requirements. You can read more about bases here: https://www1.nyc.gov/site/tlc/businesses/for-hire-vehicle-bases.page and the new High Volume FHV license here: https://www1.nyc.gov/site/tlc/businesses/high-volume-for-hire-services.page

2. Are bases decided by locations of NYC? Can there be any overlap in their coverage?
- The TLC does not dictate how the app companies divide trips between their bases, so I cannot answer your question. Any pattern, geographic or otherwise, in how ride requests are assigned to specific bases is at the discretion of the company.

3. What are the relationships between bases and rental service companies?
- We are aware that some of the app companies have partnering leasing companies that offer adjusted rates if the driver who leases the car completes a certain number of trips for that app company, etc, but that is at the discretion of the company. Bases and leasing companies are not the same, and the TLC does not license leasing companies.

Hope this helps answer some of your questions.

Inquiry: Hi, I'm checking certificate of occupancy status for Jackson Park, a multifamily development with 3 towers and 3 building IDs. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/DOB-Certificate-Of-Occupancy/bs8b-p36w I can find the certificate of occupancy details for building ID 4596920 and 4596921. But I can't find the certificate of occupancy data for building ID 4618925. Why isn't certificate of occupancy data for 4618925 showing up when I download the certificate of occupancy data?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Hi ,

This is an unfortunate side effect of a known data problem with Department of Buildings (DOB) BINs. We are working to clean this up, but here's the explanation:

Sometimes when there is new construction, our BIN data gets out of sync with the master list of BINs set by Department of City Planning (DCP). Due to issues surrounding the business process of getting permits for a new building, the building's records might be related to a "Dummy" BIN, which has an 8 as the second digit. These Dummy BINs will not show up in any other agency's data.

In this particular case, you can see on our BIS system that BIN 4618925 (http://a810-bisweb.nyc.gov/bisweb/PropertyProfileOverviewServlet?bin=4618925&go4=+GO+&requestid=0) has 2 other Dummy BINs associated with it (Additional BINs for Building). The current Certificate of Occupancy is actually tied to BIN 4856065 (http://a810-bisweb.nyc.gov/bisweb/PropertyProfileOverviewServlet?requestid=9&bin=4856065). And if you use that BIN on our Certificates of Occupancy dataset (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/DOB-Certificate-Of-Occupancy/bs8b-p36w/data), you'll see the recent history of COs there.

Another way to disentangle this issue is to look at the Borough, Block and Lot. Those may match when the BIN doesn't.

So if you're looking at the Buliding Footprints dataset (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/Building-Footprints/nqwf-w8eh), and you can't find a matching record in DOB data, this is likely the reason why. We are working closely with DCP to fix this problem.

Thank you,
- DOB Open Data Coordinator

Inquiry:
I am requesting information re: the [Violation Status] field.

If there is a null value does that mean the recipient of the citation has not challenged the citation?

All the values that do appear in the [Violation Status] field seem to indicate hearings, appeals, or some other type of claim of the recipient of the citation.
Assigned Agency's Response:
“Yes, a null or blank value in the ‘Violation Status’ field indicates that the respondent has not contested the ticket.”

Below is a brief explanation of each of the possible values that may populate the ‘Violation Status’ field.

ADMIN CLAIM DENIED: Ticket was contested, and the claim was denied administratively, without an ALJ/hearing (contested - guilty)
ADMIN CLAIM GRANTED: Ticket was contested, and the claim was denied administratively, without an ALJ/hearing (contested - guilty)
ADMIN REDUCTION: Ticket was contested, and the claim was denied administratively, without an ALJ/hearing (contested - guilty)
APPEAL ABANDONED: Original guilty determination was appealed, but the respondent never followed through with the appeal hearing (contested - guilty)
APPEAL AFFIRMED: Original guilty determination was affirmed at an appeal hearing (contested - guilty)
APPEAL MODIFIED: Original guilty determination was affirmed at an appeal hearing (contested - guilty)
APPEAL REMANDED: Case deferred, similar to an adjournment (contested - no new determination…just the original guilty)
APPEAL REVERSED: Original guilty determination was reversed at an appeal hearing (contested - not guilty)
HEARING ADJOURNMENT: Ticket was contested, and brought to a hearing. The ALJ determined that more evidence was needed. Hearing was rescheduled for another day (contested - no determination yet)
HEARING HELD-GUILTY: Ticket was contested, and found guilty by an ALJ at a hearing (contested - guilty)
HEARING HELD-GUILTY REDUCTION: Ticket was contested, and found guilty by an ALJ at a hearing, with some reduction of previously assessed penalties (contested - guilty)
HEARING HELD-NOT GUILTY: Ticket was contested, and found not-guilty by an ALJ at a hearing (contested - not guilty)
HEARING HELD-REINSTATEMENT: Ticket was found guilty at a fraud hearing (previously dismissed fraudulently) and has been reinstated (contested - guilty)
HEARING PENDING: Ticket was contested, and hearing is pending (contested - no determination yet)
HEARING WAIVED: A settlement was agreed to by the respondent, which included a waiver of ever having a hearing (not contested)


Thank you,
- NYC Open Data Team

Businesses that currently dispatch or plan to dispatch more than 10,000 for-hire vehicle (FHV) trips in NYC per day under a single brand, trade, or operating name via FHV bases must apply for the High-Volume For-Hire Service license. We do not legally differentiate between services that are primarily pooled, like Via, or sometimes pooled, like Uber and Lyft, although the congestion surcharge paid by the passenger is reduced for pooled trips. You can read more about the High-Volume For-Hire Services license, and the rules that created that license class, here: https://www1.nyc.gov/site/tlc/businesses/high-volume-for-hire-services.page

While we do not legally differentiate between the High Volume For-Hire Services company who do majority pooled versus majority non-pooled trips, all HVFHS trips are subject to new Driver Income rules, which you can read about here: https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/driver_income_rules_12_04_2018.pdf
These rules dictate that a measure of a company's utilization, defined as the percentage of time drivers are on a trip per working hour, be a factor in how much that company has to pay its drivers per trip. This will impact each HVFHS company differently, based on the utilization rate they maintain.

The dashboards are based on the FHV Base Aggregate Reports, which the TLC publishes to NYC Open Data here: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/FHV-Base-Aggregate-Report/2v9c-2k7f/data. You can find metadata available for download under the 'About' tab.

There are people who are present on both the Active & Certification datasets who have been given "Request dates" on the "Civil Service List Certification" dataset who have a high list numbers (example list numbers: 2352, 2360, 2364, 2369, 2370, 2379, 2382, 2385, 2394, 2396, 2403). While there are list numbers present on the Civil Service List (Active) dataset with lower list numbers who are not listed at all on the "Civil Service List Certification" dataset (example: 476.5, 527.5, 606.5, 1073.5, 1163.5, 1358.5, 2226, 2237, etc...). Why is that?

In another case I've actually found a person with 1 list number displayed on the Civil Service List (Active) dataset (example: 1428.500,), but the same exact person has two list numbers (same exam: 7005) on the "Civil Service List Certification" dataset (example: 603.500 and 1428.500,) who appears to have been contacted multiple times recently for both list numbers to attend a hiring pool. Inquiry: Is there an indicator for when the park was opened? How is the "TYPECATEGO" and "SUBCATEGOR" determined? What do the variables "PERMIT" and "PIP_RATABL" indicate?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Parks regarding the Parks Properties dataset.

Park Opening: The ACQUISITIONDATE is the best date to use for when a park "opened". This date indicates when the agency acquired the property. The date is not the easiest to read on the Open Data Portal but if you ignore the zeros the date appears.  For example, 19340803000000.00000 is 08/03/1934.

TYPECATEGORY: This field describes the type of property as defined by our Planning division at NYC Parks. There is a detailed list of type categories in the data dictionary (4th tab, titled "Typecategory").

SUBCATEGORY: This field defines the property as well, but the category is used by our Operations and Management Planning division (OMP). OMP is responsible for the Parks Inspection Program (PIP). You can learn more about the program here.

PIP_RATABLE: This field indicates if the property is rated as part of the Parks Inspection Program.

PERMIT: This field indicates if the property is available for reservation by permit, such as for a special event.

Thank you,
-NYC Parks and the NYC Open Data Team

Assigned Agency: Mayor's Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
Inquiry: What is the difference between adopted budget, current modified budget, and financial plan? Which is the most up to date number for what the city actually spent in a given FY?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data Help Desk. ​

​​What is the difference between adopted budget, current modified budget, and financial plan?

After an Executive Budget has been released by the Mayor, it is reviewed and revised by the City Council. If approved by the Council, the budget becomes “adopted.” The Adopted Budget is then sent back to and released by the Mayor in June.

The current modified budget is the Adopted Budget as revised through modification and approval in accordance with the City Charter.

The financial plan is an adjustment of current year expenditures and revenue forecasts and a projection of how these adjustments will affect future budgets.
The financial plan is released four times a year - one in the fall/winter, the Preliminary in January, the Executive in April, and the Adopted Budget in June.

Which is the most up to date number for what the city actually spent in a given FY?

The City Comptroller publishes a Comprehensive Annual Financial Report which details annual spending for the City. This document is available on the City Comptroller’s website.


Thank you,
- NYC Office of Management and Budget

Inquiry:
Hello! I have some questions regarding deed records in the "real property master" dataset. For context, I am grouping these records by bbl using "real property legals" and also joining party information using "real property parties":

- Why are there sometimes multiple deeds filed on one day for a given tax lot?
- When the last deed transaction date shows multiple deeds filed on the same day, how can we determine the current property owner of the tax lot?
- What does a 'docamount' value of 0 on a deed signify, specifically when the deed is filed the same day as other deeds with non-zero 'docamount' values?
-  How are 'documentid' values ordered, if at all?
Assigned Agency's Response:
The answers are as follows:


Why are there sometimes multiple deeds filed on one day for a give tax lot?
This is the nature of property sales and is controlled by the buyers and sellers and not the Department of Finance so we would not be able to list all reasons. Note that there is no requirement to record a deed when the property sells although transfer taxes returns must still be filed. With that said two common occurrences are:
Flips where party A sells the property to party B who then sells the property to party C. By looking at the document dates on the two deeds you can tell how long B help the property and often that will imply what B did with the property.
Settlement of an estate. In this case party A passes away and leaves the property to party B. Party B then only records the deed associated with this transfer then he sells to party C immediately prior to the recording for the deed from B to C.

When the last deed transaction date shows multiple deeds file on the same day, how can we determine the current property owner of the tax lot?
Generally speaking one should order by the document date from newest to oldest, next by CRFN from highest to lowest and finally by document id from highest to lowest. Note that the document id ordering is only useful for documents without CRFN which are those documents recorded prior to 1/1/2003 and brought into ACRIS from systems pre-dating ACRIS.

What does a ‘docamount’ value of 0 on a deed signify, specifically when the deed is filed the same day as other deeds with non-zero ‘docamount’ value?
As noted in the Data Dictionary for the Real Property Master dataset, the Document Amount field is the “Total Consideration for Transfers and Principal debt or obligation for Mortgages”. For deeds you can think of the Document Amount as the sales price. With this in mind, a Document Amount of 0 means the property was transferred with any money changing hands. There can be many reason for a $0 consider, but normally it means the transfer is not an “arms-length” transaction among unrelated parties. The reason most commonly associated with multiple deeds recorded the same day, some of which have non-zero consideration, is the settlement of an estate as mentioned earlier. When party B inherits the property from party A, no money changes hand; however when B sells to C, it is for a non-zero amount.


How are ‘documentid’ values ordered, if at all?
   There are three formats of Document ID in ACRIS. These are:

YYYYMMDDsssssttt = the format of documents record since 1/1/2003 where YYYY is the 4 digit year, MM is the 2 digit month, DD is the 2 digit day, sssss is a 5 digit sequence number within a day and ttt is a 3 digit sequence number within an ACRIS transaction. Document IDs in this format are assigned when the document submitter prepares the documents for recording. Documents with common ACRIS cover page transaction number, YYYYMMDDsssss, are submitted together and recorded in the order specified by sss. There is no significance to the ordering of the ACRIS cover page transaction numbers. Two submitters could prepare the documents for recording on the same day so share the YYYYMMDD portion of the document id, but could actually submit and have their documents recorded weeks or even months apart.
FT_Bssssssssssss = the format of documents whose index data was converted to ACRIS from the system immediately pre-dating ACRIS. In this format FT_ prefix is fixed, B is the property borough and ssssssssssss is a sequence number that increases with recording date.
BK_Btttttttttttt = the format of older documents whose microfilm images where indexed and imported into ACRIS. In this format the BK_ prefix is fixed, B is the property borough and tttttttttttt is a sequence number that increases with recording date. Note that BK_ documents are older than FT_ documents.
With this in mind, ordering FT_ and BK_ Document IDs has significance, but ordering Document IDs staring with 20 does not. For documents with Document ID starting with 20, use the CRFN which is a number with format YYYYrrrrrrrrr where YYYY is the year and rrrrrrrrr is a 9 digit padded sequence number which is reset each year and is monotonically increasing with recording date and time.


Regards,
DOF

Example 1: Requests to do work during an embargo period require payment of a "MISCELLANEOUS - EMBARGO WAIVER REQUEST" fee before DOT will consider the request. Inquiry: I don't understand how you determine the Poverty figures (# and %) for individual schools as it doesn't reflect our schools' Free & Reduced Lunch numbers. Can you tell me more about the source of the Poverty data?
Assigned Agency's Response:
The dataset is created by the Report and Policy Research Group.  Please feel free to contact them at  RPSGresearch@schools.nyc.gov.

NYC DOE “Poverty” counts are based on the number of students with families who have qualified for free or reduced price lunch, or are eligible for Human Resources Administration (HRA) benefits. In previous years, the poverty indicator also included students enrolled in a Universal Meal School (USM), where all students automatically qualified, with the exception of middle schools, D75 schools and Pre-K centers.

In 2017-18, all students in NYC schools became eligible for free lunch. In order to better reflect free and reduced price lunch status, the poverty indicator does not include student USM status, and retroactively applies this rule to previous years. Please note that this is different from previous years of the demographic snapshot, and so poverty data will not match earlier demographic snapshots.
Thank you,
- NYC Open Data Team

Inquiry:

Please note that summons 1005796464 was opened on "2016-12-18 11:30:00" and has no interest but a $10 penalty charged, summons number 1102218753 written on "2017-02-08 15:58:00" has a penalty of $60 and an interest charge of $21.41.

Penalty assessments do not move beyond the first penalty on summonses for which the liable owner could not be determined (as is likely the case with the cited summons 1005796464).

The NYC Department of Finance has posted on its web site a section that describes Parking and Camera Violation Penalties and Enforcement Actions. Please refer to that page for additional information.

Inquiry:
i am working on a project where I am geocoding parking tickets, parking as well as red light and speed cameras. I am using the geoclient application and Visual Basic .NET. i am getting errors where the API tells me that the roads do not intersect, but when i check on Google Maps it is apparent they do. In addition when streets have more than 2 point of intersection, the API does not provide any instructions on how to resolve that programmatically. i have screen shots that I can provide to illustrate my points.
thanks,
Assigned Agency's Response:
The Department of City Planning creates the data that supports GeoSupport and GeoSupport products like GBAT and GOAT. We can inform you how your issues are handled in those formats but GeoClient is an API created by DOITT, that use GeoSupport data, so we cannot assist in how GeoClient functions.

Regarding your first question, any intersection discrepancies between Google maps and Geosupport should be sent to GSS_feedback@planning.nyc.gov for review. Any valid intersections that are missing will be added to GeoSupport.

Regarding your second question, we can provide assistance on using GeoSupport products: GBAT and GOAT using Geosupport Function 2 (intersections).

For GOAT users, if it is a situation where two streets intersect exactly twice, you can provide a direction (North/South or East/West) to get a hit to the correct intersection.

Function 2 (intersections) have been enhanced to return a list of NodeIDs for situations where two street names intersect more than twice. This allows the user to go back into Function 2 (intersections) using NodeID instead of two street names in order to get a hit.

GBAT users of Geosupport need to use Function 2W (intersections wide), while Geosupport Desktop Edition GBAT users need to check off a box requesting Auxiliary Nodes.

Unfortunately, City Planning has no control over GeoClient. To submit feedback about GeoClient, you can try the following links:

Geoclient API: https://developer.cityofnewyork.us/api/geoclient-api

Geoclient API Feedback: https://developer.cityofnewyork.us/contact-us

Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data Help Desk. Please see agency's response below:
​
​1. We are interested in de-duplicating the dataset to measure aggregate evictions throughout the five boroughs, and there are a number of observations that have a) identical index & docket numbers or b) identical marshal name, address, date, and unit number. Do either the former or the latter indicate duplicate observations? In the former situation, it would make sense that a unique index & docket combination would refer to a unique eviction, as the index # seems to be a unique ID provided by NY Housing Court, and docket # seems to be a unique ID assigned by the marshal. However, there are cases of duplicate index & docket combination assigned to different eviction addresses, unit #s, etc. In the latter situation, we are not sure whether we can rule out the possibility of these duplicates referring to, for example, same-day evictions in different units in the same building (where a marshal might have just recorded one unit # for ease). Please advise on how we should be thinking of de-duplicating this dataset.
​
​The court assigns each eviction/legal possession case a unique index number. Docket numbers are assigned by a marshal’s office but one case may carry different docket numbers. For example, should the landlord instruct the marshal to request separate warrants for each of the respondents named in the case, each respondent will be entered as a separate docket. Some marshals add a letter “b or “c” to the docket number, which is an indication that there is more than one warrant of eviction associated to one index number. Also, an index number may be linked to different floors within the same address (Example, 2 or 3 family home occupied by an entire family or by unidentified squatters. In sum, one index number, with one or more docket numbers, is one or more eviction(s).
​
​Moreover, different county courts (Kings, Queens, Bronx, Manhattan and Richmond) may use the same index number used in other counties for different eviction cases. Some marshals may add the first letter of the corresponding county to indicate which borough it came from. In short, there can be one index number, for different addresses in different counties.
​
​2. Does this dataset constitute the universe of eviction judgments in the five boroughs from the NY Housing Courts? In other words, are there examples where eviction judgments are determined for a certain tenant that goes through NY Housing Court where a Marshal’s eviction would not automatically be scheduled and thus recorded in this dataset?

This dataset will never constitute the entire universe of “eviction judgments.”

Petitioners may obtain a court ordered judgment of eviction and, through later negotiations among the parties, the matter is settled privately without a marshal ever having been contacted by the petitioner. These private negotiations/agreements between petitioner and respondent may take place at any time (before the marshal requests the warrant, before or after the marshal serves notice, after the marshal has scheduled an eviction…)

There was one marshal who was not using the program because according to the handbook, he had a low volume of eviction cases and he did not have to be computerized. However, the marshal is no longer doing evictions.

3. Relatedly, in the ‘Schedule Status’ column of the dataset, all ~38k observations are listed as ‘Scheduled’ (in the data dictionary the column is described as either having values ‘Scheduled’, ‘Pending’, or ‘Confirmed). Assuming this is a mistake, when can we expect an update to the data in this column?

​This ‘Scheduled Status’ field should read either “Pending,” meaning not yet scheduled, or “Scheduled” meaning it’s on the marshal’s calendar. This is the way it should appear on open data. The actual scheduled date and pending evictions are not for publication due to safety reasons. The CPR has a “Confirmed” field which is an automatic confirmation, generated by the CPR system, to the marshals confirming that the next day’s eviction schedule was received by the system, no later than 4:00 pm. If they don’t receive this confirmation they do not have DOI’s approval to go forward with their evictions. This has nothing to do with public information, this is for DOI’s regulatory purposes.

4. The data come with addresses of variable accuracy and without geospatial information, which is in violation of Local Law 108 of 2015, which requires, “every public data set containing address information to utilize a standard field layout and presentation of address information and include corresponding community district and geospatial reference data.” When can standardized addresses and geospatial reference data be expected to be appended to the dataset?

There is some merit to this point. Not all datasets published in OpenData come with geospatial information. In fact, not all development teams if any are trained to include exactly what is in LL108. If this was a problem, the Open Data team would have stopped publishing any dataset and required us to make remediation steps before publishing as they are the gatekeepers and we need to adhere to certain standards. Knowing this now, I will know better going forward since we have the capability now as well. To address the present problem specific to this set, it seems clear that the requester is asking for house numbers and street numbers to be split so the dataset can be geocoded either on our side or their side. The desktop geocoder is available for the public from DCP to use, so they would need to run the dataset through that if they wanted everything. Because the law doesn’t say which reference data other than Community District, the vagueness does not help guide us to what else is needed other than having the requester self-service the rest through the desktop geocoder. It not that it isn’t available, it just won’t be easy to get ‘the rest’ of whatever the requester is seeking. So we would need the house number and street name split for us to geocode it and it is work I would assist you putting in an intake to secure this as a project enhancement. This would be the prime opportunity, if you want to proceed, to add more fields that DOI may need (e.g. case type, number of Order to show cause). I would suggest the public request revision of LL108 to be more specific on what kind of geospatial reference data. As far as I know, the address is a valid piece of information that is technically geospatial reference data already without more specifics on the definition. Here’s the actual LL108. https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/local_laws/ll108of2015.pdf

​
​Thank you,
​-NYC Department of Investigation (DOI)

Inquiry:
Good Afternoon,

I wanted to get some clarification on the “Year Built” field in PLUTO dataset. According to the data dictionary, this field represents “the year construction of the building was completed” and that it comes from “Department of Building Permits”.

I’m curious what specific type of DOB permit determines when a building has been “completed”.

I have noticed some BBLs that are included in PLUTO with “Bldg Area” and “Year Built” values that have not yet been granted a Certificate of Occupancy. For example, BBL# 4004220031 has a built year of 2016 with a 221,266 SF building listed in PLUTO even though it is an active construction site as of 7/27/18. This BBL does not even have a Temporary CO on file with DOB.

Conversely, there are buildings that were issued a Final Certificate of Occupancy in 2017 that are listed in PLUTO with a Year Built of “0”. This is the case for BBL #4004297501 which was granted a Final CO on 10/18/2017.

At what stage of construction is a building considered “completed” and what DOB permit is used to determine this? Why do some buildings have “BldgArea” values even though the “Year Built” = 0.

Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.
Assigned Agency's Response:
Year built as reported in PLUTO comes directly from the AV-YRBUILT field in DOF's RPAD Master File as stated in PLUTO's metadata. In RPAD's data dictionary AV-YRBUILT is "The year the building was built." Unfortunately, there are no other details in RPAD's data dictionary so you would have to reach out to DOF for more information regarding what determines a buildings completion and triggers the value reported in the year build field.

It's important to remember that PLUTO is a tax lot based dataset and DOF's RPAD and CAMA datasets are it's primary input datasets. PLUTO is not a building based dataset, despite the fact that it reports building based attributes and those attributes are often only the characteristics of the "primary" building. Also, lots s can remain the same, while the buildings and bins on that lot change and it can take time for the updated building information to be incorporated into DOF's data systems.

We're not exactly sure what's going on with 4004220031, but RPAD could be reporting data on the former building on the lot or newly constructed building. The information DOF collect is mostly for tax assessment.

The issue on BBL 4004297501 is potentially the result of poor data quality. Where year built is 0 it means that the year built is unknown in DOF source data.

The Department of City Planning is working to improve the data quality and QA/QC procedures for creating PLUTO. You can follow that progress here PLUTO's repo.

Thank you,
Department of City Planning

Inquiry: I recently looked at the fire dispatch and fire response data files. For the same time period 1/1/2013 to 12/31/2017 the file from Starfire Dispatch system has 135,757 records and the Incidents responded has only 117,508 which is a large difference. Shouldn't they have exactly the same number of records ? Also is there any key available to link the two files ? The response file has a 7 digit IM_INCIDENT_KEY and the dispatch file has a 16 digit Starfire_Incident_ID.I don't see any commonality between the two keys. Thanks.
Assigned Agency's Response:
All incidents are not included in the response data for a number of reasons such as….
The data for the fire dispatch dataset is derived from the Starfire Computer Aided Dispatch system. The Incidents responded dataset is derived from the NYFIRS system. They inherently collect different types of data for different purposes. The NYFIRS system is used to create incident reports, detailing some of the actions taken by fire units, for example. Not every incident as dispatched by the Starfire system requires an incident report. For example, a call that results in a false alarm may be in the Starfire dataset, but not in the NYFIRS dataset. Additionally, NYFIRS and Starfire have different categories for classifying incidents and therefore some of the counts in question may not match. These systems do not have an identifier to tie them together. However, they incidents in either dataset can be linked via the borough, alarm box number and incident datetime.

Inquiry:
According to the open data portal, the Multi-Agency permits dataset curates data on DOB Jobs permits and DOHMH permits. This dataset is reported to be updated daily, and indeed, the DOB Jobs Permits data appears to be up to date with geography listed for most recent entries. However, when filtering down to the DOHMH data, only about half of the entries have any geography associated with them, and almost none of the entries for food establishment permits that expire after 2016 have any geography associated with them. In addition to this, there are many entries across the dataset that include issuance, expiration, or status dates listed as 01/01/1900.

After looking into this issue, we have come to understand that this is likely due to the way that entries are getting updated in the dataset. If there is already a row for the permit holder in the dataset, whenever the permit is updated, a new row is created in the dataset, but only the permit holder, the permit type, and the updated fields are added to the row. All of the other fields that do not change after the update are left blank, or in the case of dates, listed as 01/01/1990. For example, if you filter the dataset to the all of the permits for Harriet’s Kitchen Inc., you would see that there are 9 entries - one for each time the food establishment permit was issued. However, only the first entry has the establishment’s permit number, issuance date, address, BBL, BIN, coordinates, and permit holder’s name. For every other entry these fields are blank or listed as 01/01/1900. For these other entries, only the permit expiration date and permit status date field gets updated.

We looked into cleaning this on our own, but unfortunately we won’t be able to. We had considered downloading the data, grouping the rows with a common food establishment permit holder name, and filling in the missing fields on newer entries with the data contained in the first entry. However, individual chain stores are often all listed under the same permit name and can have thousands of entries with missing geographic information and unique permit numbers. For instance, Domino’s Pizza LLC has over a thousand entries in dataset, and less than half have a unique license number or geographic information. In this case, we can’t know which Domino’s the row is referring to, and so we do not know, which geographic information and license numbers should be added to which entries.

At BetaNYC, in collaboration with Manhattan Borough President Gale Brewer's office, we are trying to map where food establishments with active permits are located in the city. We are doing so because we've received requests from community boards and the Manhattan Borough President's staff to make this data more accessible. This is why it will be important to us to be able to access license numbers and expiration dates on the most recent food establishment entries.
Assigned Agency's Response: The agency is in the process of preparing the data for release. The expectation is to have the dataset on the Open Data portal by 09/30/2018. Please check back then.

Assigned Agency: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH)
Inquiry:
To Whom It May Concern:

I am examining the OATH data uploaded to the NYC Open Data Portal and I have a few queries about the data.

For the hearingstatus variable, I am unable to find any information as to what some of the terms mean:
While I am aware that “ASSIGNED” means “summons had a hearing, the case is assigned, and a decision is pending but do the following mean, exactly: “ASSIGNED TO APPEALS”; “HRG BEFORE ASSIGN”; “PERFECTION REQUIRED”; “STAY REQUESTED”; “STAYED”; and STIPULATION OFFERED. For the last one, specifically, what is the difference between “STIP NEEDS REVIEW” (which means “Stipulation offered by enforcement agency (petitioner) and stipulation was accepted by respondent”) and “STIPULATION OFFERED”?

For the hearingresult variable, what does “COSRV INVIO” mean? Likewise for “POP IN-VIOL” and “SETTL IN-VIO”. I am unable to find any information on your website as to what they refer to. Also, how different are these 3 above-listed values from “IN VIOLATION” and what specifically does this mean? Are there overlaps in meaning?

Also, could you please enlighten me as to what the prefix “SAU” stands for in the scheduledhearinglocation and the decisionlocationborough variables. This prefix “SAU:” is placed before every borough. For example, “SAU: BKLN” or “SAU”MANH”.

Finally, I am not sure if this is a typo but in the violationdescription variable, besides “ASBESTOS”, “BAR”, “COMMERCIAL”, “FIRE”, “MULTIPLE DWELLING”, and “NOISE” there is the “1 -D142 2 FAMILY” value whose meaning I cannot fathom.

Thank you in advance for your time.
Assigned Agency's Response:
Thank you for contacting NYC Open Data Help Desk. Please see below the responses to your questions:
​
​For the hearingstatus variable, I am unable to find any information as to what some of the terms mean:
While I am aware that “ASSIGNED” means “summons had a hearing, the case is assigned, and a decision is pending but do the following mean, exactly: “ASSIGNED TO APPEALS”; “HRG BEFORE ASSIGN”; “PERFECTION REQUIRED”; “STAY REQUESTED”; “STAYED”; and STIPULATION OFFERED. For the last one, specifically, what is the difference between “STIP NEEDS REVIEW” (which means “Stipulation offered by enforcement agency (petitioner) and stipulation was accepted by respondent”) and “STIPULATION OFFERED”?

Assigned – Assigned to a hearing officer.
Assigned to Appeals – the summons has had an appeal filed and is with our appeals department
Hrg before assign – the summons was heard before OATH got a copy of it
Perfection Required -- An appeal has been entered but there is still paperwork that needs to be filed for the appeal to progress
Stay Requested – the respondent has filed a request to stay a case and prevent it from progressing (to default/docketing/collections etc.)
Stayed – For a variety of legal reasons (e.g., a respondent request, a hold pending some kind of negotiation or legal case), the case has a stay placed on it
Stipulation offered – this is a program that allows certain Buildings cases to be settled before a hearing subject to certain conditions. This indicator means that the offer of stipulation was sent out by OATH on behalf of the issuing agency.
Stip needs review – A respondent has accepted the offer of stipulation but for a variety of reasons, the stipulation may require intervention by OATH staff in order to be processed

For the hearingresult variable, what does “COSRV INVIO” mean? Likewise for “POP IN-VIOL” and “SETTL IN-VIO”. I am unable to find any information on your website as to what they refer to. Also, how different are these 3 above-listed values from “IN VIOLATION” and what specifically does this mean? Are there overlaps in meaning?

​​COSRV INVIO means "In Violation, Community Service Eligible" and applies only to summonses related to the Criminal Justice Reform Act (CJRA), for which community service is an available alternative to payment of a fine for an In Violation summons.
POP In Vio means "In Violation – Publicly Owned Property" – the respondent is the city itself. In these cases, the agency that owns the property isn't required to pay.
Settl In Vio means that there was a settlement prior to hearing and the respondent is recorded as having been in violation as a condition of to that settlement
​They all mean that the finding is that the respondent is in violation.
​
​Also, could you please enlighten me as to what the prefix “SAU” stands for in the scheduledhearinglocation and the decisionlocationborough variables. This prefix “SAU:” is placed before every borough. For example, “SAU: BKLN” or “SAU”MANH”.

SAU signifies that a case was assigned to the Hearings by Mail unit
​
​Finally, I am not sure if this is a typo but in the violationdescription variable, besides “ASBESTOS”, “BAR”, “COMMERCIAL”, “FIRE”, “MULTIPLE DWELLING”, and “NOISE” there is the “1 -D142 2 FAMILY” value whose meaning I cannot fathom.

​This field is used by various agencies to store various information, generally indicating something additional (a building type, a violation type) – it’s not consistent across OATH’s data. I will contact Open Data to see how they're assembling it
​
Thank you,
-Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings

Inquiry:
ubject: “Violation Status” Field and its relation to “Judgement Entry Date” field.
1- To which Violation status value “Judgement Entry Date” field is pertinent to?
(List of 15 “Violation status” we found in the data are: ADMIN CLAIM DENIED, ADMIN CLAIM GRANTED, ADMIN REDUCTION, APPEAL ABANDONED, APPEAL AFFIRMED, APPEAL MODIFIED, APPEAL REMANDED, APPEAL REVERSED, HEARING ADJOURNMENT, HEARING HELD-GUILTY, HEARING HELD-GUILTY REDUCTION, HEARING HELD-NOT GUILTY, HEARING HELD-REINSTATEMENT, HEARING PENDING, HEARING WAIVED)
2- Most of the data (about 75%) does NOT have a violation status, does this mean Violation Status field has a value only when a ticket is disputed?

3-Do you have “Violation status” workflow or Lifecycle?
Assigned Agency's Response:
1. There is no direct relationship between the JUDGMENT ENTRY DATE field and the VIOLATION STATUS field. The JUDGMENT ENTRY DATE field provides the date the violation entered into judgment status, which is based on a pre-determined penalty schedule. The VIOLATION STATUS field provides the status of a contested ticket, such as whether there is a hearing pending, or what the outcome of the hearing was. Hearings can take place both before or after the entry of judgment.

2. That is correct. Any uncontested ticket, whether it is ignored or paid, will have a blank VIOLATION STATUS.

3. There isn’t a set workflow associated with the VIOLATION STATUS values. All of the statuses, with the exception of ‘Hearing Pending’ reflect the outcome (or determination) from a hearing, whether it be an initial hearing or an appeal hearing. While there are common scenarios, the sequence of values for VIOLATION STATUS will depend on the specific case related to a disputed ticket. As an example, one common sequence might be…
‘Hearing Pending’ ---> ‘Hearing Held–Guilty’ ---> ‘Appeal Reversed’, which translates to a scenario in which a ticket was contested, found guilty at the initial hearing, and then dismissed at an appeal hearing. There are many other possibilities.

Thank you,
-NYC Department of Finance

Inquiry: if your name shows up under the "civil service list certification" what does that mean? what the certification Expiration Date mean if we did not receive a notice and what will happen to your name on this list?
Assigned Agency's Response:
A List Certification includes the names of a group of eligible candidates on an established, active Civil Service Eligible List, and it is provided to an appointing agency by DCAS to fill available positions.  The number of names on a List Certification depends on the number of available positions being filled and the number of candidates on an eligible list with identical scores.

An agency may use a given List Certification for filling positions between the date that the Certification is created and the Certification Expiration Date.  If a candidate has not received a notice it means that the agency did not use the Certification or that the candidate was not reached for consideration of appointment.  If a candidate does not receive a notice in connection with a specific List Certification, the candidate’s name remains on the underlying Eligible List and would remain available for future certifications.

Inquiry:
Thank you for responding to my previous email.

I need to calculate Net new construction using NYC Open Data, and I’d like to know if this can be done simply by subtracting Demolition of an existing Building from New Building? (i.e. Net new construction = NB-DM).

Also, would you consider Added units due to Alterations of existing buildings, which is another variable I’m working with comparable to A1, which in the NYC Open Data represents A major alteration that changes the use of occupancy of the building?

Thank you for responding to my previous email.

I need to calculate Net new construction using NYC Open Data, and I’d like to know if this can be done simply by subtracting Demolition of an existing Building from New Building? (i.e. Net new construction = NB-DM).

Also, would you consider Added units due to Alterations of existing buildings, which is another variable I’m working with comparable to A1, which in the NYC Open Data represents A major alteration that changes the use of occupancy of the building?

Thanks again for your assistance
Assigned Agency's Response:
Hi,

Net new construction isn't really something that we measure, so it's difficult to answer your question. It depends on what you're trying to measure.

If you are measuring new building structures, NB - DM could give you the net increase, so it sounds like your formula would work. I would not include A1 because it's not a change in the number of building structures. But be aware that submitting a job application or even getting a permit does not necessarily mean that the work will be completed. We are planning to add the "Sign Off" date which indicates completion of the job, but that isn't currently available in open data.

If you are instead measuring an increase or decrease in housing, you should also look at dwelling units. For this measurement, I would include A1 because that can have an increase or decrease in dwelling units. This measurement contains the same caution as above that permitting does not mean the job will be completed. It also contains a caution that the number of existing and proposed dwelling units is self-reported on the original application in our Job Application data. As the job progresses, it is possible that the plans will change and the number of units will change, but this does not get reported back to open data.

I hope that helps.

Thank you,
- , DOB Open Data Coordinator

Inquiry: Why are these population numbers different than census.gov numbers?
Assigned Agency's Response:
This data includes - unadjusted decennial census data from 1950-2000 and projected figures from 2010-2040 (summary table of New York City population numbers and percentage share by Borough, including school-age (5 to 17), 65 and Over, and total population).

Here is an explanation of possible reasons for discrepancies from the Population division at DCP:
"It is possible to get different population totals from the Census Bureau. For most recent Censuses, there were three sources --
1) the full count census;
2) a sample of the population that included more detailed information, like economic data, but included an estimate of total population;
3) a sub-sample of this sample, known as the Public Use Microdata Sample, or PUMS. (The approach changed in 2010, and now the American Community Survey has replaced the decennial sample.)

This is likely why Julie found alternative numbers at the Census Bureau site. Still, none of these three sources should differ greatly. Our recommendation is to use the full count data whenever possible, because they are the most accurate population statistics."

Thank you

Inquiry: I'd like more information about one of the variables. The codebook is a little thin on the matter. The variable is INITIAL_SEVERITY_LEVEL_CODE. how exactly are these assigned? They appear to be lower numbers are higher priorities, but this is not explicit. Is the same method used in all years, months, cases? etc. Ideally, I'd like to be put in touch with someone with intimate knowledge of this particular data set. Thank you!
Assigned Agency's Response:
When someone calls 9-1-1 and reaches an EMS Alarm Receipt Dispatcher (ARD), the ARD asks a number of questions to triage the call and determine its type and severity. This is determined through a computer algorithm that acts as a decision tree to find a call type through previous responses. Our EMS ARDs are also trained EMTs and they have the ability to override the computerized triage algorithm.

The call type determines which what type of resource the incident will receive. In our case, it will receive an Advanced Life Support (ALS) ambulance, a Basic Life Support (BLS) ambulance, a DUAL response (ALS+BLS) and in some cases a Certified First Responder (CFR) response. CFRs include all of our Fire Engine companies.

Each call type is mapped to a severity level. The severity level determines which incidents will get an unit assigned to the incident first. Severity levels 1-3 (also called segments) are categorized as life-threatening emergencies. 4-8 are non-life threatening emergencies. Note that not all of the highest priorities have the same type of response.

Each incident will have an initial and final severity level and call type because it can be important to know how the incident was originally triaged (based on the information the first caller gave) and how that categorization may have changed base on new information from additional callers or other trained personnel on scene or changes in patient condition, for example.

I hope this is helpful.

Inquiry:
Hi, I have questions regarding the csv files taken from your website:
www.nyc.gov/html/dot/downloads/misc/fatality_yearly.csv
www.nyc.gov/html/dot/downloads/misc/injury_yearly.csv

1. What does MVOInjurie exactly include? does it include motorcyclists injuries?
2. What does BikeInjurie exactly include? does it include motorcyclists and/or electric bikes?
3. What is the exact definition of an injurie? does it include "light" cases without hospitalizing?
4. Is it possible to get geolocation data about the motorcycles injuries and fatalities in NYC?
5. Is it possible to get geolocation data about the vehicles (without motorcycles) injuries and fatalities in NYC?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Greetings,

Please see below answers to your questions:

1. What does MVOInjurie exactly include? does it include motorcyclists injuries? - This category includes injuries to anyone inside or on a motor vehicle that occurred during a traffic crash. It includes motorcycles.

2. What does BikeInjurie exactly include? does it include motorcyclists and/or electric bikes? - This category includes injuries to anyone on a bicycle that occurred during a traffic crash with a motor vehicle. No it does not include motorcyclists or electric bicyclists.

3. What is the exact definition of an injurie? does it include "light" cases without hospitalizing? - All injury levels are included, hospitalization is not required.

4. Is it possible to get geolocation data about the motorcycles injuries and fatalities in NYC? - DOT’s crash data is a summary of NYPD data and we group all motor vehicles (motorcycle, auto, truck, etc.) in one count. Individual crashes from NYPD are available at https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/NYPD-Motor-Vehicle-Collisions/h9gi-nx95;
you can filter on the Vehicle Type Code columns.

5. Is it possible to get geolocation data about the vehicles (without motorcycles) injuries and fatalities in NYC? - (same answer as #4)

Thank you,
-NYC Department of Transportation
-NYC Open Data

Inquiry: What is the logic for the sign codes in the signs.csv file (eg PS-65C, SP-477B, etc)? Do you have a guide/legend to help decipher what Sign Description the codes represent?
Assigned Agency's Response:
Greetings,

The sign code is a unique identifier for a sign design, and it generally has one sign description. As an example, SP-477B sign description is “BUS STOP SIGN (BUS & HANDICAP SYMBOLS) NO STANDING W/ SINGLE ARROW”. DOT does not maintain a separate guide/legend of sign codes. Excel pivot tables or other software can summarize the list of codes and their descriptions, if desired.

For most signs, all sign instances with the same sign code are physically the same. However, there are several exceptions where sign text can vary. “SPECIAL,” “INSERT” AND “RIDER” are examples of such codes. “SPECIAL” signs are often used for events, or for ceremonial street renaming, and “INSERT” AND “RIDER” are used for signs that appear on or below other signs. These generic codes have fallen out of use at DOT, but the data still contains examples.

DOT also uses generic sign codes for Bus Stop route, destination and locator panels, for some speed limit signs, and in several other cases. These sign codes have descriptions that indicate there is a variable element to the sign. An example would be the bus stop route sign, with the description “LOCAL MTA BUS ROUTE PANEL (TEXT TO BE MODIFIED AS REQUESTED)” or a speed limit sign, with the description “SPEED LIMIT XX SPEED CHECKED BY RADAR (XX = SPEED TO BE DETERMINED).”


Thank you,
-NYC Department of Transportation

Assigned Agency's Response:
According to this dataset's Data Dictionary, "tree_dbh" represents the diameter of the tree, measured at approximately 54" / 137cm above the ground. Because standard measuring tapes are more accessible than forestry-specific measuring tapes designed to measure diameter, users originally measured tree circumference in the field. Both the field measurement and processed value were rounded to the nearest whole inch.

You are trying to find permits for roof replacement. This isn't something that we regularly report on, so it's not a simple thing. Here's how you can do it:

First, look for the job applications that include roof replacement work in our DOB Job Application Filings dataset by filtering the Job Description field for "roof". From what I can see, these are usually Alt 2 jobs, but that might not always be the case. This field is typed in by the applicant and there is no standardization, so you may want to make your filter narrower by using "roof replacement" or "roof replace", but you might be excluding "replace the roof", so you'll have to play with this filter until you are satisfied with the results.
Use the Job # field and cross reference with the DOB Permit Issuance dataset. Note: In the permit dataset, you may get several permits for a single Job #. You should look at the Work Type and Permit Type fields to narrow down to the exact permit that you want. For example, the entire alteration job might include both roof replacement and plumbing work, and you don't want the PL (Plumbing) Work Type permit.
That should get you to the report that you are looking for. If you have any additional questions, please let me know.

Uber/Lyft drivers who have a TLC license would be included in the Livery category, but certain ride types licensed in surrounding states would not need a TLC license to operate, therefore they would fall into the regular categories depending on the vehicle type if involved in a crash.

a) SEDN – Passenger Vehicle
b) SUBN – Sport utility vehicle/station wagon
c) VAN – Van
d) PICK – Pick-up Truck
e) SCOM – Small commercial vehicle (four tires) (e.g., box truck, etc)
f) LCOM – Large commercial vehicle (six or more tires) (e.g., semi, tractor-trailer, etc.)
g) TAXI – Taxi vehicle
h) LIV – Livery vehicle
i) BUS – Bus
j) AMBU – Ambulance
k) FIRE – Fire truck
l) MCY – Motorcycle
m) SCOOT – Scooter
n) BIKE – Bicycle
o) PCAB – Pedicab
p) UNK – Unknown
q) OTH – Other

Thanks,
NYC Open Data
